text:
sam_infra: Heads-up: EU-west GPU pools at >=95% for the last 45m. Queue backlog spiking on several low-priority routes. Seeing a big embed/chat-lite burst from partner X, anyone on call?

maria_ops: I'm on it. Looks like 3 tenants sending long-running generation jobs. Tail latency SLOs creeping up for premium routes.

jon_enginfra: Can you paste the admission stats? Are we being hit by long sequences (KV cache misses) or raw QPS?

maria_ops: QPS spike on `embed-bulk` and `chat-lite`. avg seq length on chat-lite jumped ~2x. Quick dump: 
```
route: chat-lite qps: 420 -> 1200
route: embed-bulk qps: 80 -> 400
gpu_util: 96%\nqueue_depth_total: 980
```

niya_sre: I'm worried about starvation if we switch to strict priority-only. We've seen premium churn before when low-priority floods and we preempt warm pools.

sam_infra: Agreed. Two high-level proposals:
- Proposal A: per-route weighted fair-queueing with aging (protects small premium QPS but still lets long-running requests age into service).
- Proposal B: burst throttles + per-tenant rate limits + global overflow FIFO for best-effort traffic (simpler to implement).

tomas_prod: Can we hybridize? e.g., strict priority for premium routes, per-route buckets for standard/internal, and a small FIFO overflow queue with tail-drop for best-effort. That keeps guarantees for paying customers and bounded complexity.

jon_enginfra: Implementation cost: weighted fair queue needs per-request weight computation and token accounting (adds memory/CPU). Simpler change is admission controller flags: `route_priority` + `age_boost_seconds`. Might get 80% of benefits with much less code.

maria_ops: Here's a config prototype I sketched for hybrid mode:
```
admission_control:
  mode: hybrid
  per_route: true
  priorities:
    premium: 100
    standard: 50
    best_effort: 10
  age_boost_seconds: 30
  overflow_policy: fifo_drop_oldest
```

niya_sre: Two operational concerns:
1) Priority inversion during model cold-starts or when shards are rebalanced (we might queue premium requests but still stall on I/O).
2) Billing/customer-facing issues — customers will see 429s without context unless we expose clear headers/logs.

sam_infra: For (1) we can reserve a tiny warm pool for premium and add a fallback to a compatible quantized variant for standard routes. For (2) we should return `429` with `x-rw-throttle-reason` and a link to docs plus metrics to explain the throttle.

tomas_prod: Also add an observability metric: `queue_age_percentile{route}` and `admission_rejected{route,reason}` so product/CS can trace customer impact.

deploy-bot: deploy request: admission/hybrid v0.3 by sam_infra to staging queued.

maria_ops: I'll run synthetic burst tests in staging (30m runs with A/B profiles) and collect p50/p95/p99 for premium vs standard. If staging looks good, canary to eu-west for 30m during low traffic window.

jon_enginfra: If we detect starvation in canary, fallback plan: revert to FIFO and enable per-tenant fair-share for 1 hour while we iterate. Need rollback automation.

niya_sre: I'll update the runbook with thresholds and paging rules: page if GPU util >85% + queue_depth_total > 500 for >5m. Also add a synthetic job to exercise the age_boost path.

sam_infra: Action items recap: maria -> staging tests and metrics, jon -> rollout/rollback plan + lightweight instrumentation, niya -> runbook + alerts, tomas -> add queue-age metrics and `admission_rejected` counters. I'll open a PR for the config schema and a short design doc. :thumbsup:

maria_ops: One tiny note — let's ensure we don't leak tenant IDs in 429 bodies. Use opaque codes and internal logs only.

tomas_prod: ack.

sam_infra: Thanks all. If we get green on staging I'll start the canary tonight. Keep threads here for updates.
